admissible.reading: Two 16 x 16 mm drive lugs retained 4 mm inward, at x=156..160; original +x torque and all other inputs retained.
admissible.why: Named drive lugs leave depth open. Admit these local 4 mm solids; unchanged 64 mm couple arm gives +/-625 N. Added mass is disclosed, not the acceptance criterion.

spec.name: Shaft bracket in torsion

supports.note: Rigid attachment to gearbox across entire x=0 face.

loads.note: Total +625 N along z over top lug; 64 mm separation gives 40 N m torque about +x.
Total -625 N along z over bottom lug; equal and opposite to top lug force.

passive.note: 16 x 16 mm end-face lug; assumed 4 mm axial depth inside envelope.
16 x 16 mm end-face lug; assumed 4 mm axial depth inside envelope.

spec.description: 160 x 80 x 80 mm shaft bracket; y is up. Entire x=0 face clamped to gearbox. End drive lug patches span y=64..80 and y=0..16, z=32..48 at x=160. Equal/opposite z forces of 625 N at y=72 and y=8 give +40000 N mm torque about x with zero resultant force. Assume each lug extends 4 mm into the envelope as a preserved solid. Volume fraction 0.3 applies to non-passive design volume.

admissible.reading: Two 16 x 16 mm drive lugs retained 2 mm inward, at x=158..160; original +x torque and all other inputs retained.
admissible.why: Same named-lug interpretation as row 1, with 2 mm depth. Both load footprints and +40 N m torque remain correct; do not generalize to unrelated retained material.

spec.name: Shaft bracket in torsion

supports.note: Rigidly bolted x=0 end: fix all three translations across the end face.

loads.note: Top lug bounds y=64..80, z=32..48 at x=160. F=40000/(72-8)=625 N; top force +z gives +x torque.
Bottom lug bounds y=0..16, z=32..48 at x=160. Equal opposite -z force, net force zero and net torque +40000 N mm.

passive.note: Preserve the 16 x 16 mm top drive lug footprint; assume 2 mm axial thickness (one element).
Preserve the 16 x 16 mm bottom drive lug footprint; assume 2 mm axial thickness (one element).

spec.description: 160 mm x 80 mm x 80 mm shaft bracket; y up. Fully fixed gearbox interface at x=0. At x=160, 16 x 16 mm top and bottom drive lugs centered at z=40 carry a pure +x torque of 40 N m: +625 N along z on the top lug and -625 N along z on the bottom lug (64 mm centroid separation). Assume isotropic steel E=210000 N/mm^2, nu=0.3 and 2 mm axial depth for solid drive lug pads.

admissible.reading: Two 16 x 16 mm drive lugs retained 4 mm inward, at x=156..160; original +x torque and all other inputs retained.
admissible.why: Confirms row 1: identical physical specification after ignoring names and descriptive text. Local depth of the named lugs is unspecified.

spec.name: Shaft bracket in torsion

supports.note: Entire x=0 end rigidly bolted to gearbox; fix all translations.

loads.note: Top lug y=64..80, z=32..48 at x=160. +625 N along z; pair separation 64 mm gives +40000 N*mm about x.
Bottom lug y=0..16, z=32..48 at x=160. -625 N along z, balancing top force and producing +x torque.

passive.note: Preserve top 16 x 16 mm drive lug; assumed 4 mm axial depth within envelope.
Preserve bottom 16 x 16 mm drive lug; assumed 4 mm axial depth within envelope.

spec.description: 160 x 80 x 80 mm shaft bracket, y up. Clamp x=0. Apply +40 N*m about x through equal opposite z forces on 16 x 16 mm end-face drive lugs. Assume 4 mm axial solid lug depth within envelope and isotropic linear-elastic steel E=210 GPa, nu=0.3.

notes: 40 N*m = 40000 N*mm; the lug centres are 64 mm apart, so a 625 N couple in z. M_x = r_y F_z: the top lug (r_y = +32) pushes +z.

adjudication.comment: Lug centres y=72 and 8 give 64 mm separation; +/-625 N gives +40000 N mm. FEAD citation is incomplete.
